title: Three-Week IB Business Management Revision Plan
summary: IB Business Management revision plan for November: use three focused weeks to triage topics, practise exam questions, time papers and protect your rest.
body_markdown:
November exam preparation rarely begins with an empty calendar. Other subjects are competing for attention, coursework may still need polishing, and three weeks can feel uncomfortably short.


The answer is not to study Business Management all day. A useful **IB Business Management revision plan** divides the remaining time into three jobs: diagnose weaknesses, convert knowledge into exam-ready answers, and rehearse complete papers under timed conditions. Most students can make meaningful progress with 60-90 focused minutes on ordinary days, two longer sessions each week, and protected recovery time.


This plan works for SL and HL students. Adjust the session length around your other November subjects, and always follow the examination documents and schedule provided by your school.


### The three-week plan at a glance


Week Main priority What you should produce


Week 1 Topic triage and knowledge repair A ranked weakness list, refreshed concepts and short question practice


Week 2 Application, calculations and evaluation Marked responses, an error log and stronger answer structures


Week 3 Timed paper rehearsal and recovery Completed simulations, final corrections and a calm exam-day routine


Start by opening the[IB Business Management resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-business-management) . Keep one document or notebook as an error log throughout all three weeks. Every mistake should become a specific action, not a vague instruction to revise harder.


### Week 1: Find the marks you are currently losing


The first week is diagnostic. Students often begin by rereading their favourite unit because familiarity feels productive. The more valuable move is to locate the topics that would cost marks if the exam were tomorrow.


### Days 1-2: Run a topic triage


Rate each syllabus area using three labels:


- **Red:** you cannot explain or apply the material without help.
